info.text:
A stock fortune can grow for decades with zero income tax, and the gain can disappear at death. This video explains, with 2026 numbers, how the realization rule, lower long-term capital gains rates, borrowing against assets, and the step-up in basis work together, all under current law. A worked example shows two people with the same $100,000 paying $20,820 versus $5,167.50 in federal tax, plus a hypothetical $10 million buy, borrow, die example. We also explain why studies put the richest Americans' tax rate at 8.2% or 3.4%, and why critics dispute those numbers.
